_comment: Free-text {{TEXT_*}} placeholders. kind: line (single line) | text (multi-line) | number (positive integer). A TEXT_ is optional: left empty, the line that carries it is removed. Set mandatory: true only where the instruction cannot exist without it.

TEXT_PROJECT_NAME.label: Project name
TEXT_PROJECT_NAME.fill_in: Document the project or service name and, optionally, the assessment identifier using project-specific information.
TEXT_PROJECT_NAME.required: a concise, non-secret name that uniquely identifies the engagement.

TEXT_QUESTIONS_AND_RULES.label: Specific questions, critical workflows and business rules
TEXT_QUESTIONS_AND_RULES.fill_in: Document specific questions, critical workflows and business rules using project-specific information.
TEXT_QUESTIONS_AND_RULES.required: clear, testable questions and expected invariants, without secrets.
TEXT_QUESTIONS_AND_RULES.example: Can a standard user approve a payment above the configured limit?.

TEXT_AUTHORIZATION_TEST_CASES.label: Specific authorization test cases
TEXT_AUTHORIZATION_TEST_CASES.fill_in: Document explicit authorization test cases using project-specific information.
TEXT_AUTHORIZATION_TEST_CASES.required: acting label, target, action, expected decision, policy source, safe prerequisites and cleanup for each case.
TEXT_AUTHORIZATION_TEST_CASES.example: USER_A attempts to read ORDER_B; expected DENY per access matrix row 12.

TEXT_APPLICATION_DESCRIPTION.label: Application description and main workflows
TEXT_APPLICATION_DESCRIPTION.fill_in: Document the application or API purpose and principal workflows using project-specific information.
TEXT_APPLICATION_DESCRIPTION.required: a project-specific description of users, business purpose, main flows and important trust boundaries.
TEXT_APPLICATION_DESCRIPTION.example: Customer portal for invoice submission, review and approval.

TEXT_OTHER_API_TYPE.label: Other API style
TEXT_OTHER_API_TYPE.fill_in: Document an API style selected as other using project-specific information.
TEXT_OTHER_API_TYPE.required: a precise description of the interface, transport, framing and contract artifacts.
TEXT_OTHER_API_TYPE.example: custom TCP message protocol documented in protocol-v2.pdf.

TEXT_API_ENVIRONMENTS_AND_VERSIONS.label: API environments and lifecycle status
TEXT_API_ENVIRONMENTS_AND_VERSIONS.fill_in: Document API environments, versions and lifecycle status using project-specific information.
TEXT_API_ENVIRONMENTS_AND_VERSIONS.required: active, deprecated, staging, production and shadow versions, with base paths and status.
TEXT_API_ENVIRONMENTS_AND_VERSIONS.example: v2 active in staging; v1 deprecated but in scope for read-only checks.

TEXT_API_DEPENDENCIES.label: API trust boundaries and dependencies
TEXT_API_DEPENDENCIES.fill_in: Document API trust boundaries and dependencies using project-specific information.
TEXT_API_DEPENDENCIES.required: gateways, upstream and downstream services, callbacks and third-party integrations, including scope status.
TEXT_API_DEPENDENCIES.example: API Gateway routes to Orders Service; payment provider is out of scope.

TEXT_AUTHORIZATION_MODEL.label: Authorization model
TEXT_AUTHORIZATION_MODEL.fill_in: Document the expected authorization design using project-specific information.
TEXT_AUTHORIZATION_MODEL.required: roles, scopes, ownership rules, tenant boundaries, policy source and decision points; distinguish documented from inferred rules.
TEXT_AUTHORIZATION_MODEL.example: customers access only owned orders; tenant admins access orders in their tenant.

TEXT_ACCESS_MATRIX.label: Expected access-control matrix
TEXT_ACCESS_MATRIX.fill_in: Document the expected access-control matrix using project-specific information.
TEXT_ACCESS_MATRIX.required: actors or roles versus functions, resources, actions, ownership and tenant context, with allow or deny decisions and policy source.
TEXT_ACCESS_MATRIX.example: USER_A may read ORDER_A but must be denied access to ORDER_B.

TEXT_CRITICAL_BUSINESS_FLOWS.label: Critical business flows
TEXT_CRITICAL_BUSINESS_FLOWS.fill_in: Document business flows with material authorization impact using project-specific information.
TEXT_CRITICAL_BUSINESS_FLOWS.required: ordered workflows, actors, assets, invariants and potential consequences.

TEXT_FUNCTIONALITY_CRITICALITY.label: Functionality criticality
TEXT_FUNCTIONALITY_CRITICALITY.fill_in: Document the criticality of functions under test using project-specific information.
TEXT_FUNCTIONALITY_CRITICALITY.required: function-level business impact and rationale, distinguishing security from availability or usability concerns.
TEXT_FUNCTIONALITY_CRITICALITY.example: payment release: critical; profile display: medium.

TEXT_ADDITIONAL_RESOURCES.label: Additional workspace resources
TEXT_ADDITIONAL_RESOURCES.fill_in: Document additional workspace resources and when to use them using project-specific information.
TEXT_ADDITIONAL_RESOURCES.required: file names or references, their purpose, authority and consultation point; exclude secrets.
TEXT_ADDITIONAL_RESOURCES.example: Architecture.md for trust boundaries; roles.csv for expected permissions.

TEXT_AUTHORIZED_TARGETS.label: Authorized targets and testing window
TEXT_AUTHORIZED_TARGETS.fill_in: Document the exact authorized testing targets and window using project-specific information.
TEXT_AUTHORIZED_TARGETS.required: precise URLs, hosts, ports, paths, repositories, branches, accounts, tenants, environments and approved window as applicable.

TEXT_ACCOUNTS_AND_ROLES.label: Accounts, roles and tenants
TEXT_ACCOUNTS_AND_ROLES.fill_in: Document designated test identities and authorization context using project-specific information.
TEXT_ACCOUNTS_AND_ROLES.required: non-secret account labels, roles, privilege tiers, tenants, ownership context, permitted workflows and restrictions.
TEXT_ACCOUNTS_AND_ROLES.example: USER_A: customer in TENANT_A; ADMIN_A: tenant administrator.

TEXT_ACCESS_PROCEDURE.label: Credential access and login procedure
TEXT_ACCESS_PROCEDURE.fill_in: Document the approved credential and access procedure using project-specific information.
TEXT_ACCESS_PROCEDURE.required: how to obtain credentials securely, log in, complete MFA, renew sessions, log out and recover access; never include reusable secrets.
TEXT_ACCESS_PROCEDURE.example: Retrieve credentials from the approved vault, complete MFA, and use isolated browser profiles.

TEXT_TEST_DATA.label: Authorized synthetic test data and ownership
TEXT_TEST_DATA.fill_in: Document authorized synthetic test data and ownership using project-specific information.
TEXT_TEST_DATA.required: approved records, identifiers, owners, allowed mutations, cleanup requirements and prohibited real data.
TEXT_TEST_DATA.example: ORDER_A owned by USER_A; creation and deletion allowed in staging.

TEXT_API_DEFINITION.label: API contract or machine-readable definition
TEXT_API_DEFINITION.fill_in: Document the machine-readable API contract using project-specific information.
TEXT_API_DEFINITION.required: artifact name, format, version and location for OpenAPI, GraphQL SDL, WSDL/XSD, proto or equivalent.

TEXT_VALID_REQUESTS_JSON.label: Valid-request corpus
TEXT_VALID_REQUESTS_JSON.fill_in: Document the sanitized valid-request corpus using project-specific information.
TEXT_VALID_REQUESTS_JSON.required: representative valid requests per operation with method, target, headers, parameters, body, role, sequence and expected response class; exclude secrets.
TEXT_VALID_REQUESTS_JSON.example: valid-requests.json covering create, read, update and delete operations.

TEXT_API_CLIENT_COLLECTION.label: Client collection and environment
TEXT_API_CLIENT_COLLECTION.fill_in: Document the approved API client collection and environment using project-specific information.
TEXT_API_CLIENT_COLLECTION.required: collection format, file reference, non-secret variables, base URLs and usage limitations.

TEXT_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.label: Endpoint and operation inventory
TEXT_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.fill_in: Document the authorized endpoint and operation inventory using project-specific information.
TEXT_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.required: versions, methods or operations, administrative and batch functions, jobs, webhooks, callbacks and authorized undocumented interfaces.
TEXT_ENDPOINT_INVENTORY.example: GET /orders/{id}, POST /orders, admin batch export and order-status webhook.

TEXT_EXPECTED_RESPONSES.label: Expected responses and error model
TEXT_EXPECTED_RESPONSES.fill_in: Document the expected success and error model using project-specific information.
TEXT_EXPECTED_RESPONSES.required: expected status or response classes, schemas, error semantics and relevant side effects for safe comparison.
TEXT_EXPECTED_RESPONSES.example: 200 for owned objects, 403 for cross-tenant access, standardized error body.

TEXT_API_WORKFLOWS.label: Business-flow and sequencing rules
TEXT_API_WORKFLOWS.fill_in: Document API business flows and sequencing rules using project-specific information.
TEXT_API_WORKFLOWS.required: ordered operations, prerequisites, state transitions, invariants and safe cleanup steps.
TEXT_API_WORKFLOWS.example: create cart, add item, submit order, cancel before fulfilment.

TEXT_ENGAGEMENT_CONTACTS.label: Engagement contacts and stop authority
TEXT_ENGAGEMENT_CONTACTS.fill_in: Document engagement contacts, test window and stop authority using project-specific information.
TEXT_ENGAGEMENT_CONTACTS.required: owner and escalation roles, approved window, communication channel and person authorized to stop testing; avoid unnecessary personal data.
TEXT_ENGAGEMENT_CONTACTS.example: Application owner via SEC-ENG channel; testing window defined in change ticket.
